modules.description: Kroppsdeler og grunnleggende anatomi som er nyttig i helse- og omsorgssituasjoner.
Vanlige symptomer, plager og sykdomstegn du kan møte i helse- og omsorgsarbeid.
Skader, kroniske tilstander og andre helseproblemer som er viktige å kunne beskrive.
Ord og uttrykk for personlig stell, hygiene, smittevern og daglige omsorgsoppgaver.
Ord for ernæring, væske, søvn, mobilitet, forflytning og toalettbehov.
Enkle og nyttige spørsmål og beskjeder i møte med pasienter, brukere og barn.
Uttrykk for å spørre, forklare, innhente samtykke og skape trygghet.
Ord og uttrykk om barn, utvikling, trivsel, støtte og beskyttelse mot skade og omsorgssvikt.
Yrkesroller, arbeidssteder og vanlig utstyr i helse-, omsorgs- og oppvekstsektoren.
Sentrale begreper om profesjonell omsorg, etikk, dokumentasjon og samarbeid.
Ord og uttrykk for sikkerhet, førstehjelp og handling i akutte situasjoner.
Ord for observasjon, vitale tegn, rapportering og grunnleggende legemiddelrelatert språk.

words.example: Did you hit your head when you fell?

words.english: Please keep pressure on the wound.
words.definition: an instruction used to help control bleeding by maintaining pressure
words.example: Please keep pressure on the wound while I call for help.

words.definition: an instruction to remain with someone who needs observation, reassurance, or help
words.example: Stay with the person until help arrives.

words.definition: watch carefully in order to notice important information or changes
words.example: Observe the patient’s breathing and skin color.

words.definition: observe or measure something over time to detect changes
words.example: Monitor the patient’s condition.

words.definition: give important information to another person, often a colleague or supervisor
words.example: Report any sudden change in the patient’s condition.

questions.prompt: You must _____ a sudden change in the patient’s condition.

words.definition: make a written or digital record of important information
words.example: Document what you observed and what action you took.

words.definition: a noticeable difference in a person’s physical or mental health
words.example: Report a sudden change in condition immediately.

words.definition: basic measurements that show important body functions
words.example: Temperature, pulse and breathing are examples of vital signs.

words.definition: the measured heat level of the body
words.example: A normal body temperature varies between people and during the day.

words.definition: the rhythmic beating felt in an artery as the heart pumps blood
words.example: Check the pulse and record the result.

words.definition: the force of blood pushing against the walls of the arteries
words.example: The nurse measured the patient’s blood pressure.

words.definition: the amount of glucose present in the blood
words.example: The patient checks their blood sugar regularly.

words.definition: the percentage of hemoglobin in the blood that is carrying oxygen
words.example: The nurse checked the patient's oxygen saturation.

words.definition: the number of breaths a person takes in one minute
words.example: Record the breathing rate along with the other vital signs.

words.definition: a gas the body needs for normal cell function and that may also be given as medical treatment
words.example: The patient is receiving oxygen through a nasal tube.

words.definition: a substance used to prevent, treat or relieve illness or symptoms
words.example: Medication must be handled according to workplace routines.

words.definition: a medical order for a medication or treatment, or the document containing that order
words.example: The medication requires a prescription.

words.definition: a measured amount of medication intended to be taken or given at one time
words.example: Always check the prescribed dose before medication is given.

words.definition: an unwanted effect that can occur when using a medicine or treatment
words.example: Report a possible side effect according to workplace routines.

words.definition: a medication used to reduce or relieve pain
words.example: The patient asked whether a pain reliever was available.

words.definition: difficulty thinking clearly, understanding, remembering, or knowing where you are
words.example: Sudden confusion can be an important change in condition.

words.definition: damage to skin and underlying tissue caused by prolonged pressure or pressure combined with friction
words.example: Regular repositioning can help prevent a pressure ulcer.
